$comment: The Waterloo campaign's battles (designed 17 to 18 Oct 2026; see the Grognards Campaign Design doc). Maps use the authored glyphs (. open, : farmland, * woods, ^ hill, # buildings; roads as '='), river specs as js/water-core.js reads them, and place names as [name, x, y, kind] in board cell units. Objectives are text for now; their machine conditions come with the objective engine.
name: The Waterloo Campaign

battles.name: Ligny
battles.history: Napoleon attacked Blücher's three corps strung along the Ligny brook, and the villages of Saint-Amand and Ligny changed hands all afternoon. At dusk the Imperial Guard broke the Prussian centre at Ligny, but Gneisenau led the army away north in good order, which let it march to Waterloo two days later.

Prussia.start: Rows 6 to 10; may start in the villages

objective.text: At the end of round 12, two Brigades unbroken and Blücher (Zieten's Brigadier) in play.

brigades.name: Zieten, under Blücher
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery

brigades.name: Pirch
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Light Cavalry

brigades.name: Thielmann
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Heavy Cavalry, Artillery

objective.text: Hold two of Ligny's village squares at the end of round 12, or break one Prussian Brigade.

brigades.name: Vandamme
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Gérard
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Heavy Cavalry, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Imperial Guard
brigades.note: Brigadier, Guard x3, Artillery

battles.special: The Imperial Guard cannot move before round 5.
battles.balance: France has the Guard and 3 more points, but must cross the brook (one bridge, two fords) into villages, and its Guard only has six rounds. Prussia only has to survive in shape, which a careful player can do, so its margin is thin troops spread over three villages. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Saint-Amand
battles.history: On the French left, Vandamme's corps and later the Young Guard fought Zieten's and Pirch's Prussians for the three villages of Saint-Amand, Saint-Amand-la-Haye and Wagnelée. The French ended the day holding Saint-Amand, while the Prussians kept Wagnelée.

Prussia.start: Rows 5 to 10; one Brigade must start in Saint-Amand

objective.text: Hold Wagnelée, or a square of Saint-Amand-la-Haye, at the end of round 10.

brigades.name: Steinmetz
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3 (one fewer for balance)

brigades.name: Tippelskirch
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery

objective.text: Hold two squares of Saint-Amand at the end of round 10.

brigades.name: Vandamme
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery (+Infantry, Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Young Guard (Duhesme), arrives round 4 on row 1
brigades.note: Brigadier, Guard x2, Infantry

battles.balance: Even on points. France faces houses behind water but gets the Young Guard as a second wave once Saint-Amand is softened; Prussia can fall back village by village and only needs to keep the rear one. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Blücher Unhorsed
battles.history: As the Guard broke through at Ligny, the 73-year-old Blücher led a cavalry counter-charge in person. His horse was shot and fell on him, and French cuirassiers rode past him twice in the dusk while his aide Nostitz stood guard, before Prussian lancers drove them off and he was carried away.

Prussia.start: Blücher at E6; the rest rows 8 to 10

objective.text: Blücher in play and in rows 8 to 10 at the end of round 8.

brigades.name: Blücher's escort
brigades.note: Blücher (to protect), Light Cavalry x2, Infantry x2

objective.text: Remove Blücher, or have two units in rows 8 to 10, at the end of round 8.

brigades.name: Milhaud
brigades.note: Brigadier, Heavy Cavalry x2, Guard (+Heavy Cav for balance)

battles.special: Blücher is pinned for rounds 1 and 2, then moves as cavalry and cannot attack.
battles.balance: Even on points. The cuirassiers reach him by round 2, so the Prussian lancers must screen him and then race him four squares home; France can also win by pushing through, which pulls Prussia two ways. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Quatre Bras
battles.history: Ney attacked the Quatre Bras crossroads, held at first only by Dutch-Belgian troops, while Wellington fed in Picton's division, the Brunswickers and finally the Guards as they arrived. By nightfall the Allies still held the crossroads, but Ney had kept Wellington from helping Blücher at Ligny.

Britain.start: Perponcher in columns I to P; Picton arrives round 3 and Brunswick round 5 on column T

objective.text: Hold a square of the Quatre Bras crossroads hamlet at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Perponcher (Dutch-Belgians)
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery

brigades.name: Picton, round 3
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Guard

brigades.name: Brunswick, round 5
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Light Cavalry

France.start: Columns A and B; Kellermann arrives round 4 on column A

objective.text: Hold Gemioncourt at the end of round 12, or remove four Allied units.

brigades.name: Bachelu
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Foy
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Light Cavalry (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Kellermann, round 4
brigades.note: Brigadier, Heavy Cavalry x3

battles.special: Reinforcements enter on their own end at the start of the round shown.
battles.balance: France has 28 points against Perponcher's 14 for the first two rounds and should take Gemioncourt; the Allies catch up to 40 against 42 as reinforcements arrive near the crossroads. Both objectives were met on the day. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Kellermann's Charge
battles.history: Late in the afternoon Kellermann led his cuirassiers through the tall rye at Halkett's brigade. The 69th Foot, ordered out of square into line, was ridden down and lost a colour; the cuirassiers reached the crossroads before artillery and musketry broke them.

Britain.start: Rows 5 to 7, in and around the rye

objective.text: Remove two French cavalry units by the end of round 6.

brigades.name: Halkett
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x4 (the 69th starts in line), Artillery

objective.text: Break an Allied battalion and get a unit onto the crossroads (F9), both by the end of round 6.

brigades.name: Kellermann
brigades.note: Brigadier, Heavy Cavalry x3, Light Cavalry

battles.special: Tall rye: a unit in farmland is hidden from enemies more than two squares away.
battles.balance: Even on points. Cavalry beat infantry in line but lose to squares and guns; the rye decides who is caught out. Short and sharp. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: The Duke's Narrow Escape
battles.history: Riding forward to watch the Brunswickers, Wellington and his staff were caught by French lancers and chasseurs. He galloped for the 92nd Highlanders, told them to lie down, and jumped his horse over their bayonets into the square. Close by, the Duke of Brunswick was shot leading his men and died that evening.

Britain.start: Wellington at C4; the 92nd in square at G8; Brunswick rows 5 and 6

objective.text: Wellington ends round 4 next to or inside the 92nd's square, and is in play at the end of round 8.

brigades.name: Wellington and the 92nd
brigades.note: Wellington (to protect), Infantry (the 92nd, in square), Infantry (a Brunswick battalion)

brigades.name: The Duke of Brunswick
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry, Light Cavalry

objective.text: Remove Wellington or the Duke of Brunswick by the end of round 8.

brigades.name: Piré
brigades.note: Brigadier, Light Cavalry x3, Infantry (+Light Cav for balance)

battles.special: Wellington moves as cavalry and cannot attack; a square shelters a commander standing in it.
battles.balance: Britain has 2 more points but two commanders to keep alive, and Wellington starts three squares from safety with lancers two moves away. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: The Cavalry at Genappe
battles.history: Wellington fell back from Quatre Bras in a thunderstorm, Uxbridge's cavalry covering the retreat. In Genappe's narrow street the 7th Hussars charged the French lancers and were thrown back; then the 1st Life Guards came down the hill and drove the lancers through the town, and the pursuit slowed.

Britain.start: Rearguard columns E to H; Uxbridge on the Heights of Genappe (columns M to P)

objective.text: Have three units leave by the Brussels end by the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Rearguard
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Artillery

brigades.name: Uxbridge
brigades.note: Brigadier, Heavy Cavalry x2, Light Cavalry x2 (one is the 7th Hussars)

objective.text: Remove three Allied units by the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Subervie
brigades.note: Brigadier, Light Cavalry x3, Heavy Cavalry (+Light Cav for balance)

brigades.name: Advance guard
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Artillery

battles.special: Thunderstorm: no artillery fire in rounds 1 to 4, and all ground but roads costs one extra move. The Dyle is crossed at the bridge or the ford.
battles.balance: Even on points. The Allies must squeeze through one bridge with French cavalry behind them; the Life Guards on the heights are there to counter-charge and buy the time. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Wavre
battles.history: While the rest of the Prussian army marched to Waterloo, Thielmann's single corps held the line of the Dyle at Wavre, Bierges and Limale against Grouchy's far larger force. Grouchy forced a crossing at Limale and drove Thielmann back on the 19th, but by then Waterloo was lost, and his 33,000 men had spent the battle away from it.

objective.text: Hold three squares of Wavre (N5 to Q6) at the end of round 8.

brigades.name: Thielmann
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery

brigades.name: Stulpnagel
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Light Cavalry

objective.text: Hold one of the three bridgeheads on the Prussian bank at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Vandamme
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x4, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Gérard
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery (+Artillery for balance)

brigades.name: Pajol
brigades.note: Brigadier, Light Cavalry x2, Heavy Cavalry

battles.special: The Dyle is crossed only at bridges. Five artillery hits destroy a bridge.
battles.balance: France has 43 points against 25, but every attack goes over a two-square bridge, Prussia can blow a bridge with its guns, and Prussia's clock stops at round 8. Limale (the wooden bridge, furthest from Wavre) is the weak point, as it was. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Hougoumont
battles.history: The walled chateau-farm of Hougoumont, in front of Wellington's right, was held all day by the Guards' light companies, Nassauers and Hanoverians against Prince Jérôme's and later Foy's divisions. Once, the French broke in at the north gate, and were killed to a man after Macdonell and a handful of Guardsmen forced it shut.

Britain.start: In the chateau (D5 to E6), the garden and the orchard; the guns on the ridge (rows 8 and 9)

objective.text: Hold all four chateau squares (D5, E5, D6, E6) at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Macdonell
brigades.note: Brigadier, Guard x2, Infantry (Nassau), Artillery

objective.text: Enter a chateau square at least once, and remove one Allied unit, by the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Jérôme
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x4, Artillery

battles.special: French waves: a lost French Infantry unit returns on row 1 two rounds later, up to four times.
battles.balance: France has 17 points plus up to 12 more in waves against 16 in stone buildings. The garden and orchard are the outworks France must take first. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: La Haye Sainte
battles.history: Major Baring's 2nd Light Battalion of the King's German Legion held the farm of La Haye Sainte on the Brussels road all afternoon, with the 95th Rifles in the sandpit opposite. Their Baker rifles needed special ammunition that never arrived, and at about six the French took the farm; 42 of nearly 400 defenders got back to the ridge.

Britain.start: Baring in the farm (F5, F6); the 95th in the sandpit (H5); the rest on the ridge (rows 8 and 9)

objective.text: Hold a farm square until the end of round 8, and have Baring in play at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Baring (King's German Legion)
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2

brigades.name: Kempt
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Artillery

objective.text: Hold a farm square at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Donzelot
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x4, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Travers
brigades.note: Brigadier, Heavy Cavalry x2

battles.special: From round 7 the units in the farm cannot volley (their rifle ammunition is gone).
battles.balance: France has 27 points against 19, but the farm is stone and the sandpit flanks the road. The ammunition rule tips it to France late, which is the history: the farm holds for hours, then falls. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Papelotte
battles.history: On Wellington's far left, Prince Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar's Nassauers held the hamlets of Papelotte, La Haye and Smohain against Durutte's division all day. In the evening Zieten's Prussians arrived from the east and, seeing the Nassauers' dark uniforms, at first fired on them, before the two joined up and the French were driven off.

Britain.start: In the hamlets (Papelotte F5 to G6, La Haye K6 to L7, Smohain R5 to S7)

objective.text: Hold two of the three hamlets at the end of round 10.

brigades.name: Saxe-Weimar (Nassau)
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

Prussia.start: Arrives round 6 on column T, rows 5 to 7

objective.text: Three units next to Nassau units at the end of round 10.

brigades.name: Zieten
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Light Cavalry

objective.text: Get into any of the three hamlets by the end of round 6.

brigades.name: Durutte
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x4, Artillery (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: Jacquinot
brigades.note: Brigadier, Light Cavalry x2

battles.special: Mistaken identity: on the round they arrive, Prussian units cannot attack and cannot be supported by Nassau units. From Britain's route the AI commands Zieten; from Prussia's, Saxe-Weimar.
battles.balance: France has 25 against 14 for five rounds and only needs one hamlet briefly; the Allies need two at the end, which the Prussians make possible from round 6. Target 50 to 60% for each side.

battles.name: Plancenoit
battles.history: From half past four, Bülow's Prussians came out of the Bois de Paris and attacked Plancenoit, behind the French right. Lobau's corps, then the Young Guard and finally two battalions of the Old Guard retook the village in turn, and the fighting around its walled churchyard went on until the Prussians took it for good at about half past eight.

Prussia.start: Rows 8 to 10, out of the Bois de Paris

objective.text: Hold the church, or four village squares, at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Hiller
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery (+Infantry for balance) (+Artillery for balance)

brigades.name: Ryssel
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Light Cavalry (+Infantry for balance)

France.start: Lobau in the village; Duhesme rows 1 to 3; the Old Guard joins Duhesme on row 1 in round 6

objective.text: Hold the church (K5) at the end of round 6.

brigades.name: Lobau
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Artillery

brigades.name: Duhesme (Young Guard)
brigades.note: Brigadier, Guard x2, Infantry; the two Old Guard battalions (Guard x2) join in round 6

battles.balance: France has 32 against 28 and starts in the houses, but its clock ends at round 6; Prussia must still be in the village at round 10 after the Old Guard arrives. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: Waterloo
battles.history: Wellington held the ridge of Mont-Saint-Jean all day, with Hougoumont and La Haye Sainte in front of it, through the grand battery, d'Erlon's attack and Ney's massed cavalry charges. As the Prussians broke into the French right at Plancenoit, the Imperial Guard's final attack was thrown back, and the French army fell apart.

Britain.start: Rows 7 to 10, with one unit each in Hougoumont (B6, C6), La Haye Sainte (K6) and Papelotte (Q6, R6)

objective.text: No French unit on Wellington's ridge, and Hougoumont still held, at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Maitland and Halkett
brigades.note: Brigadier, Guard x2, Infantry x2, Artillery

brigades.name: Picton and Ponsonby
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x2, Heavy Cavalry x2, Artillery

Prussia.start: Arrives round 6 on column T, rows 3 to 5

objective.text: Three units in rows 1 to 3 at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Bülow
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Light Cavalry

objective.text: La Belle Alliance (K1) still French at the end of round 9, and Napoleon in play at the end of round 12.

brigades.name: Reille
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Artillery x2 (+Infantry for balance)

brigades.name: d'Erlon and Milhaud
brigades.note: Brigadier, Infantry x3, Heavy Cavalry x2

brigades.name: Imperial Guard
brigades.note: Napoleon (to protect), Guard x3, Artillery

battles.special: The Imperial Guard cannot move before round 7. From Britain's route the AI commands Bülow; from Prussia's, the two British Brigades.
battles.balance: Coalition 52 (38 from the start) against France 53. France can win outright by taking the ridge, but its own objective is to hold its centre and get Napoleon out, which becomes hard once Bülow arrives. Target 50 to 60% each.

battles.name: The Pursuit to Genappe
battles.history: Gneisenau drove the Prussian cavalry and every infantryman who could still march after the beaten French through the night. At Genappe the road jammed with guns and wagons; Prussian fusiliers took Napoleon's own carriage, and the Emperor escaped on horseback minutes before.

objective.text: Reach the carriage square (H5) by the end of round 10.

brigades.name: Gneisenau
brigades.note: Brigadier, Light Cavalry x2, Heavy Cavalry, Infantry (Keller's fusiliers) (+Light Cav for balance)

France.start: Columns E to K; Napoleon at J5

objective.text: Napoleon in the last two columns at the south end at the end of round 6.

brigades.name: Rearguard
brigades.note: Napoleon (to protect), Guard x2, Infantry, Artillery

battles.special: Night: artillery fires only at targets within two squares. The jammed road: road squares give no extra move in columns F to L.
battles.balance: Prussia has 15 against 16. Napoleon has a head start of five squares but must cross the bridge; the rearguard must either cover him or the carriage, not both. Target 50 to 60% each.

intro: June 1815. Napoleon is back from Elba and has marched north into Belgium to strike Wellington's Anglo-Allied army and Blücher's Prussians before they can join. Four days decide the fate of Europe.
